title: Your HIDDEN German pension:
body: Swipe – it's in the table on slide 4.

title: Many expats think the money stays in Germany.
body: India and Germany have a social security agreement.
Your German pension can be paid to your bank account in India.
foot: Agreement between India and Germany on social security, in force since 1 October 2017.

title: How it works
body: - 1 year at the average German salary (€51,944) = about €42.52 pension a month
- Earn more = more pension per year
- Highest possible: about €83 a month per year (salary from €101,400)
foot: Pension value from 1 July 2026: €42.52. Average salary 2026 (provisional): €51,944. Contribution ceiling 2026: €101,400 a year.

title: Find your years

after: Columns = your yearly salary before tax. Cells = German pension a month, before tax and health insurance.

foot: Example in today's euros: same yearly salary every year, pension value 2026. Real amounts depend on your full record. Not a guarantee.

title: The rules
body: - You need at least 5 years of contributions in Germany
- The pension starts at retirement age (67 for most of us) – not when you leave
- Tax rules for the payout depend on where you live then
foot: Deutsche Rentenversicherung. General information, no tax advice.

title: Your German colleague vs. you
body: - German colleague: starts at 25, works 42 years here
- You: start here at 30, maybe stay 10–15 years
- Same job, same salary – but a much smaller German pension
Plan the gap early: company pension, new pension depot from 2027, or property.

title: Recap
body: - Your German pension is not lost when you move back
- Min. 5 years, paid from retirement age
- Close the gap while you still earn in euros
